q: What happened when Russian forces launched a punitive campaign against the Makhosh, a Circassian tribe, in 1828?
gold: On 8 September 1828 Major General Antropov launched a punitive campaign against the Makhosh villages. With his detachment and allied Nogai princes he made a surprise attack on Makhosh villagers who were plowing their fields. The Makhosh had their rifles with them: the outermost were overwhelmed by the Cossack cavalry charge without resistance, while those further in regrouped and fired volleys, but the Cossack cavalry ultimately killed the remaining Makhosh.

q: According to the Tractatus de ortu Tartarorum, what did the Russian bishop Peter tell the pope about the Mongols' armies and plans?
gold: Peter could not estimate their numbers but said many nations and members of all religions had joined them. Their forces were active on three fronts, against Egypt, the Turks, and the Hungarians and Poles; they meant to bring their armies together in Syria and their ultimate goal was world conquest. He praised their military abilities: excellent archers, women who were also warriors, impenetrable leather armour and excellent siege engines. They crossed rivers on horseback and were preparing ships in three locations.

q: How did the Lisbon parish of Beato get its name, and what part did it play in the conspiracy of 1640?
gold: A man who died in 1602 with a reputation for holiness was called Beato António by the people; he gave his name to the Convent of Beato António, later shortened to Beato, the district's name. In 1640 Xabregas-Beato was one of the most active centres of the conspiracy against Spanish rule; one of the noble conspirators, D. Gastão de Sousa Coutinho, had his palace there, and in 1644 he built a chapel to Nossa Senhora da Restauração (Our Lady of Restoration) near it.

q: Where did the 1929 play Houseparty have its tryouts before Broadway, and who produced it?
gold: Houseparty was produced by A. L. Erlanger and George C. Tyler, the first original production of their new partnership. Its first tryout was at Parsons Theatre in Hartford, Connecticut, on 2 September 1929; the local reviewer was impressed with the writing, acting and staging but thought it ambitious for two neophyte writers with an unsympathetic neurotic protagonist. After four performances it moved to the Shubert Theatre in New Haven on 5 September 1929 for three more days of tryouts.

q: When did the Wolverhampton and Walsall Railway open, and how did it become part of the Midland Railway?
gold: The line opened for passengers, and probably goods, on 1 November 1872, worked by the LNWR with eight or nine return passenger trains. The W&WR had secured a commitment from the LNWR to route the relevant goods traffic over it, but the LNWR diverted traffic over its own lines, and the W&WR sought a court order. The line passed to the Midland Railway with effect from 1 August 1876, ratified by the Midland Railway (Further Powers) Act 1876 of 11 August 1876.

q: How many US war resisters were in Canada according to the War Resisters Support Campaign, and what happened to some who went back to the US?
gold: Between 30 and 40 US war resisters, some with families, were in contact with the Campaign and applying for refugee status; the best estimate of all US war resisters in Canada was 100 to 200. q: What happened to Marcus Grönholm at the 2007 Rally Ireland, and what did it mean for the championship?
gold: Grönholm won the first special stage, in front of Stormont Castle in Belfast, on the Thursday evening. On the Friday, in the fourth stage, he hit a wall hard; he and co-driver Timo Rautiainen were taken to hospital as a precaution and, though unhurt, withdrew. Sébastien Loeb (Citroën) won the rally and retook the lead of the drivers' standings, a step towards his fourth world title; Mikko Hirvonen finished fourth.

q: What is the Belgian sculptor Jules Lagae best known for, and how did his career develop?
gold: Lagae's best-known early work is the bust of the poet Guido Gezelle commissioned by Hugo Verriest, the only work of art Gezelle had made while alive and the model for all later Gezelle busts; Lagae also cast Gezelle's death mask. He took lessons at the Roeselare academy from age nine and met the sculptor Clément Carbon at fourteen. In 1896 he broke through with three monumental commissions: for the Botanical Garden in Brussels, a statue in Mechelen and the Ledeganck Monument in Eeklo. In 1900 he came second in the competition for the Golden Spurs Monument in Kortrijk. Later works include the statue of Guido Gezelle in Bruges (1930).

q: Why is the Leonidas neighborhood of New Orleans also called Pigeon Town, and where does the name Leonidas come from?
gold: The informal name Pigeon Town has its roots in the word pidgin, a simplified speech used between people with different languages, and has been passed down through generations. Leonidas may come from the Spartan king, but more likely from Leonidas Street, possibly renamed after Reconstruction for Leonidas Polk, the Episcopalian 'fighting bishop'. Bienville began a plantation in the area around 1719; the first house was built in 1835, and the area was part of the town of Carrollton.

q: What role did the city of Ḫubišna (Cybistra) play in Hittite history?
gold: Before the Hittite period Ḫubišna was a strategic hub guarding the northern end of the Cilician Gates, on the route south to Tarsus. According to the Telepinu Proclamation, Labarna I, the 17th-century BCE founder of the Hittite Old Kingdom, conquered it and appointed his sons as its rulers. In the 16th century BCE King Ammuna campaigned to re-subjugate it among other states that had revolted against Hittite rule.

q: How did the Confederates stop Admiral Porter's gunboats on Deer Creek during the Steele's Bayou expedition in 1863?
gold: Brigadier General Winfield S. Featherston's brigade was ordered to the Rolling Fork-Deer Creek junction, and Brigadier General Stephen D. Lee added one of his regiments. From 20 March the first Confederates arrived under Lieutenant Colonel Samuel W. Ferguson: an infantry battalion, six field guns and 40-50 cavalry. They felled trees across Deer Creek to block the flotilla. Porter sent about 300 sailors ashore under Lieutenant Commander John M. Murphy, who held an Indian mound and let the gunboats creep to within half a mile of Rolling Fork, but Ferguson renewed the attack on 21 March.

q: How did the Brazilian Navy come to buy the torpedo boat Goyaz, and what happened to it in the 1924 naval revolt?
gold: Goyaz was built by Yarrow as Jeanne, a sister of Caroline, which the Russian Empire had bought through intermediaries as a supposed yacht and turned into the torpedo boat Lástochka. After that scandal the police watched Jeanne and she could not be sold to Russia; she came to the attention of the Brazilian Naval Commission in Europe. In the 1924 revolt the rebel crew, under fire, grounded at São Francisco Cove and raised the white flag; Army artillery and machine guns attacked it, and it was escorted back after a Navy launch reached it, and its crew were taken prisoner to the Naval Battalion.

gold: The Order of Hermes is divided into Houses. Ex Miscellanea, Flambeau, Jerbiton and Tytalus are social Houses. Bjornaer are shapeshifters of a Germanic tradition, each with a Heartbeast, and form a Mystery Cult. q: What did the ballet teacher Nadine Wulffius contribute to ballet in Western Australia?
gold: Wulffius founded her own ballet school in Maddington, Western Australia. She was one of Kira Bousloff's first helpers at the West Australian Ballet and its ballet mistress for 12 months. She built the spirit of a corps de ballet, teaching relaxation and breath control, body stance, lifting the diaphragm and eye exercises, and specialised in head and refined arm movements; her hand movements were based on those of the Estonian dancer Ella Ilbak. q: What dinosaur fossils have been found in Ruyang County in Henan, China?
gold: Since 2005 a dense distribution of dinosaur fossils has been found in Ruyang County: six relatively complete skeletons and over 90 fossil sites. Six kinds are known: the Ruyang Yellow River Giant, giant sauropods, medium sauropods, armoured ankylosaurs (the Luoyang Zhongyuan dinosaur), bird-like dinosaurs and large carnivorous theropods. The Ruyang Yellow River Giant, excavated at Liufugou Village in Liudian Township, is 18 metres long and 6 metres high at the shoulder, the largest known dinosaur in Asia.

q: What are the safety hazards of detonation spraying with a D-gun?
gold: The D-gun reaches about 4,000 °C and uses flammable, explosive fuels, generally acetylene, to make the supersonic shockwave, so there is a serious burn and explosion hazard: no one should be in the room while it runs, the room should withstand a malfunction, and protective gloves should be used for the gun and hot parts. Dust and fumes from the feedstock can cause silicosis (silica), siderosis (iron), metal fume fever (copper, zinc, magnesium, aluminium), and some inconclusive studies link aluminium exposure to Alzheimer's.

q: What happened in the 1973 collision between the tanker Esso Brussels and the container ship Sea Witch in New York Harbor?
gold: On 1 June 1973 the Esso Brussels anchored in the southernmost anchorage of The Narrows, loaded with 319,402 barrels of light Nigerian crude for Exxon's Bayway Refinery, with a crew of 37 under Captain Constant Dert. The outbound container ship Sea Witch lost its steering and, at about 13 knots with engines in full reverse, rammed the tanker's starboard side between the deckhouses, piercing three cargo tanks and locking the ships together. The spilled crude caught fire, engulfing both ships in burning oil, and the tanker's crew abandoned ship into the one available lifeboat.

q: Who founded the PREDA Foundation in the Philippines, and what has it done for Fil-American (Amerasian) children?
gold: PREDA was founded in Olongapo City in 1974 by Father Shay Cullen, an Irish Columban missionary priest from Dublin, with Alex Corpus Hermoso and Merly Ramirez; Cullen has been nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize twice. PREDA social workers organised an association of 720 mothers of Fil-American children, helped with family research and in 1993 pursued a class action suit in a US court in Washington, D.C. on the children's behalf. It lobbied Congress and the State Department, which led to a congressional resolution assigning $650,000 for them through USAID; in 2012 it spoke out on the 52,000 Amerasians without legal recognition.
